newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: CRICKET-ENGLAND IN LATE INROADS VS NZ IN 1ST TEST.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-ENGLAND IN LATE INROADS VS NZ IN 1ST TEST.

text.p: England fought their way back into the first cricket test against New Zealand with a good final session on the opening day at Eden Park on Friday.
After being sent in to bat, New Zealand were 233 for five at the close, with Stephen Fleming on 58 and Chris Cairns on 15.
The first two sessions belonged to New Zealand.
Openers Bryan Young and Blair Pocock got through to lunch at 72 without loss. By tea, New Zealand had lost just two wickets, Young for 44 and Adam Parore for six.
However, from 154 for two at the second interval, New Zealand lost their way as Pocock, Nathan Astle and Justin Vaughan went out in the space of 13 overs.
Pocock, recalled after a 2-1/2 year absence, made his highest score in 13 test innings, 70 off 197 balls, including eight boundaries.
Both Pocock and Vaughan went out leg before wicket, as had Young earlier in the day.
Fleming played some elegant strokes, including lofting left-arm spinner Phil Tufnell for six over long on.
He had made his 11th half century in 39 test innings, and was aiming to complete his maiden hundred on Saturday.
Cairns had a reprieve on five, when he slapped an Alan Mullally full toss low to mid off where Darren Gough spilled the possible catch.
Dominic Cork was the pick of a disappointing England bowling attack, finishing with two for 53 off 21 overs, while Mullally, Gough and Craig White picked up one wicket apiece.
